column1: Title
column5: Preconditions
column6: Steps
column7: Expected Result

column1: Verify the Work Orders settings tab lists all Work Order setting toggles in order
column5:
1. You are signed in as an Admin at https://sv7301.qa.shopview.com.
2. You can reach Administration.
column6:
1. Go to /administration/settings.
2. Click the 'Work Orders' tab.
3. Read the list of settings top to bottom.
column7:
1. The Work Orders tab lists these toggles top to bottom: Auto-approve Lines, Require Vendor Invoice Number, Require Review Before Completion, Require Tech Story, Require Mileage, Require Engine Hours, Automatically Pick Inventory Parts.
2. Each toggle shows an On/Off switch and its current state, with a short description underneath.
3. There is no 'operating mode' (Full vs Simple) selector anywhere on the page.
4. The toggles appear as one plain list (there is no special 'new' styling separating them from older settings).

column1: Verify there is no operating-mode selector and no VIN-required setting on the Work Order settings page
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Read the whole Work Orders settings tab top to bottom.
2. Look for a 'Mode' or 'Full vs Simple' selector.
3. Look for a 'Require VIN' or 'VIN required' toggle.
column7:
1. There is no operating-mode (Full vs Simple) selector.
2. There is no 'Require VIN' toggle among the Work Orders settings.
3. Behavior is driven only by the individual toggles listed on the tab.

column1: Verify a 'Create Purchase Orders' toggle exists on the Work Orders tab and controls the Vendor Invoice setting
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Look on the Work Orders settings tab for a 'Create Purchase Orders' toggle.
2. If it exists, turn it Off and watch the Require Vendor Invoice Number setting.
3. Turn it back On and watch the Require Vendor Invoice Number setting.
column7:
1. A 'Create Purchase Orders' toggle is present on the Work Orders tab (default On).
2. With 'Create Purchase Orders' Off, the Require Vendor Invoice Number setting is hidden.
3. With 'Create Purchase Orders' On, the Require Vendor Invoice Number setting is shown.

column1: Verify the Require Vendor Invoice Number toggle is present with helper text and drives Optional vs Required completion
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Locate the 'Require Vendor Invoice Number' toggle.
2. Read its helper text.
3. Note its current On/Off state.
column7:
1. The 'Require Vendor Invoice Number' toggle is present on the Work Orders tab.
2. Its helper text reads exactly: 'When on, parts and a vendor invoice number are required to complete a work order. When off, complete now and receive parts later.'
3. Its On/Off state matches requireVendorInvoiceNumber in GET /api/organizations/settings.

column1: Verify Auto-approve Lines ON approves a work-order line the moment it is added
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Auto-approve Lines is set to ON and saved.
3. An open work order is on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Click New Line.
2. Fill in a canned line and Save.
3. Observe the new line's approval state.
column7:
1. The new line is created.
2. The line is immediately Approved.
3. No 'Needs Approval' / Approve-Decline prompt is shown for the line.

column1: Verify Auto-approve Lines OFF leaves a new line in Needs Approval with Approve/Decline actions
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Auto-approve Lines is set to OFF and saved.
3. An open work order is on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Click New Line.
2. Fill in a canned line and Save.
3. Observe the new line's approval state and actions.
column7:
1. The new line is created.
2. The line shows a 'Needs Approval' state.
3. Approve and Decline actions are available on the line.

column1: Verify existing settings (tech story, mileage, engine hours, auto-pick) display the org's current values
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
3. GET /api/organizations/settings values are known for this org.
column6:
1. Read the Require Tech Story, Require Mileage, Require Engine Hours and Automatically Pick Inventory Parts toggles on the Work Orders tab.
2. Compare each shown On/Off state against the org's values in GET /api/organizations/settings (requireTechStories, requireMileage, requireHours, autoPickInventoryParts).
column7:
1. Each of these four toggles is shown on the Work Orders tab.
2. Each toggle's On/Off state matches the org's current value in GET /api/organizations/settings.
3. Simply viewing the tab does not change any value.

column1: Verify first-use defaults on a brand-new org (auto-approve OFF, create POs ON, vendor invoice REQUIRED)
column5:
1. A brand-new organization that has never edited Work Order settings is available.
2. Signed in as that org's Admin.
column6:
1. Open /administration/settings → Work Orders tab for the new org.
2. Read the default state of Auto-approve Lines, Create Purchase Orders, and Vendor Invoice.
column7:
1. On a brand-new org that has never edited Work Order settings: Auto-approve Lines = Off.
2. Create Purchase Orders = On.
3. Require Vendor Invoice Number = On (required).

column1: Verify saving a settings change persists after page reload
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
3. Note the current state of one toggle (e.g. Require Engine Hours).
column6:
1. Flip one toggle (e.g. Require Engine Hours) to the opposite state.
2. Click Save Settings.
3. Reload the page.
4. Re-read the toggle. (Restore it afterward to leave the org unchanged.)
column7:
1. Save Settings completes without error (POST /api/organizations/settings/change).
2. After reload the toggle keeps the new state.
3. GET /api/organizations/settings reflects the new value.

column1: Verify a settings change applies to future completions and to a completed work order when it is reopened, but not retroactively to work orders left completed
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order was already completed under the previous settings.
3. You can change a Work Order setting.
column6:
1. Complete a work order under the current Work Order settings so it reaches Complete.
2. Go to the Work Orders settings tab, change a relevant setting (for example turn Require Review Before Completion ON) and Save.
3. First, without touching the completed work order, check its status.
4. Then reopen the completed work order (for example add a New Line, which returns it to Approved) and complete it again.
5. Observe whether the new setting now applies to the reopened work order.
column7:
1. While it is left completed, the already-completed work order still shows Complete and is not changed by the new settings (the change is not applied retroactively to work orders that stay completed).
2. Only work orders completed after the change follow the new settings for their first completion.
3. When the completed work order is reopened, the new settings now apply to it: re-completing it must satisfy the new gate (for example it now routes through the review step / Ready for Review instead of completing directly).
column8: SV-7696 (S1-R9 (future completions + apply on reopen; never retroactive to WOs left completed))

column1: Verify a non-admin user cannot see or modify the Work Order settings
column5:
1. A user without the App Settings permission (e.g. Service Advisor or Technician) exists for this org.
2. You can sign in as that user.
column6:
1. Sign in as a role without the App Settings permission (e.g. Technician).
2. Try to open /administration/settings and reach the Work Orders tab.
3. Try to save a Work Order setting change (including a direct API save via POST /api/organizations/settings/change).
column7:
1. The role without App Settings cannot reach the Work Orders settings (redirected away by the app).
2. That role cannot save Work Order settings.
3. The backend rejects a Work Order settings save from that role with HTTP 403.

column1: Verify the settings model contains no operatingMode field and no requireVin setting
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin with API access.
2. You can call GET /api/organizations/settings.
column6:
1. Call GET /api/organizations/settings.
2. Inspect the returned object keys for 'operatingMode'.
3. Inspect for a 'requireVin' Work Order setting.
column7:
1. There is no operatingMode field in the settings object.
2. There is no requireVin Work Order setting exposed.
column8: SV-7696 (S1 AC (no requireVin / no operatingMode field))

column1: Verify the Save Settings button is only enabled when there is an unsaved change
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab with no pending changes.
column6:
1. With no changes made, look at the Save Settings button.
2. Flip a toggle and look at the Save Settings button again.
column7:
1. Saving changes with the 'Save Settings' button persists the settings.
2. It is acceptable in v1 for 'Save Settings' to stay enabled even with no unsaved change (there is no dirty-state gating; this is a low-priority polish, not a blocker).

column1: Verify the Require Review Before Completion toggle is present on the settings page and drives the review flow
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Locate the 'Require Review Before Completion' toggle.
2. Turn it On and Save.
3. Start completing a work order and observe the completion CTA.
column7:
1. The 'Require Review Before Completion' toggle is present on the Work Orders tab.
2. With it On, completing a ready work order uses the review flow: the primary action becomes 'Send To Review' and the work order goes to 'Review' with a 'Ready for Review' indicator instead of completing immediately.
3. (For a work order that still has parts to order or receive, the button stays 'Complete Work Order' and opens the completion wizard first.)

column1: Verify every Work Order setting toggle has descriptive helper text
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. On /administration/settings → Work Orders tab.
column6:
1. Read each toggle's supporting description text.
2. Confirm each explains what On vs Off does.
column7:
1. Every Work Orders toggle has a short description under it.
2. Each description explains what turning the toggle On or Off does, in plain language.

column1: Verify a Complete Work Order button appears next to New Line on the work order
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order with at least one approved line is on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Look at the work order Lines toolbar.
2. Locate the New Line button.
3. Locate the Complete Work Order button.
column7:
1. A 'Complete Work Order' button is present.
2. It sits near the New Line action on the work order.

column1: Verify a work order with no parts completes in one confirm and reaches the Success screen
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order with a single labor-only, approved line exists (no parts).
3. Required-field settings for this org are known (e.g. Require Mileage ON).
column6:
1. On the work order Lines tab, click Complete Work Order.
2. If a tech-story modal appears first, enter a story and click Continue.
3. In the Details step, enter any required fields (e.g. Mileage).
4. Click Complete Work Order in the wizard.
column7:
1. There is no PO / receive / invoice step for a no-parts work order (wizard = Details → Success).
2. The Success screen appears reading 'Order complete' and 'Sent to Finance as an invoice-ready draft'.
3. All lines move to Completed and the work order status becomes Complete.

column1: Verify the Success screen shows the work order number and total with Done and Go to Invoice actions
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You have just completed a work order and are on the Success screen.
column6:
1. Read the work order number on the Success screen.
2. Read the total shown.
3. Identify the Done and Go To Invoice buttons.
column7:
1. The Success screen shows the work order number (e.g. S2-15747).
2. It shows the invoice total (e.g. $382.77).
3. Both a Done and a Go To Invoice button are present.

column1: Verify Go to Invoice from the Success screen opens the Finance step where the invoice number is shown
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are on the Success screen of a just-completed work order.
column6:
1. Click Go To Invoice.
2. Observe the destination screen.
3. Look for the invoice number.
column7:
1. You are taken to the Finance / invoice step for that work order.
2. The invoice number is shown on the Finance step (not on the Success screen).

column1: Verify completion is blocked when a required vehicle field is missing
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Mileage (or another required field) is ON.
3. An open work order with an approved line and NO mileage recorded is ready to complete.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. In the Details step, leave the required field (e.g. Mileage) empty.
3. Attempt to confirm completion.
column7:
1. Completion is blocked while the required field is empty.
2. The user is prompted to supply the missing required field.
3. Completion proceeds only after the required field is filled.
column8: SV-7697 (S2-R2 / S2 AC (missing required fields blocked))

column1: Verify with Create POs OFF a work order with vendor parts completes with no PO, no vendor bill and no AP sync
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Create Purchase Orders is set to OFF.
3. An open work order with an approved vendor-part line exists.
column6:
1. Complete the work order in one confirm.
2. Check whether any PO was created.
3. Check for any vendor bill / AP sync.
column7:
1. No purchase order is created for the vendor part.
2. No vendor bill and no accounts-payable sync happen.
3. The vendor/found part is received at request time only (no catalog or inventory sync).
column8: SV-7697 (S2-R6 / S2 AC (Create POs off ⇒ no PO))

column1: Verify in-stock inventory parts decrement inventory and write Part History on simple completion
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order has an approved in-stock inventory part line.
3. Note the part's current on-hand quantity.
column6:
1. Complete the work order via the simple (skip) flow.
2. Check the inventory on-hand quantity for that part.
3. Check the part's Part History.
column7:
1. The in-stock part's on-hand quantity decrements by the used amount.
2. A Part History entry is written for the movement.
3. The skip path does not bypass inventory movement / Part History.

column1: Verify with Auto-pick Inventory OFF the completion modal requires picking parts before Complete
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Automatically Pick Inventory Parts is OFF and saved.
3. An open work order with an approved inventory-part line exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the Pick step in the completion modal.
3. Try to continue without picking, then pick and continue.
column7:
1. A Pick step appears offering 'Pick all from default bins' and 'Review individually'.
2. You cannot complete until inventory parts are picked.
3. After picking, completion can proceed.
column8: SV-7697 (S2-R2 / S2 AC (auto-pick off ⇒ pick in modal))

column1: Verify adding a new line to a completed work order returns it to Approved
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order is in Complete status.
column6:
1. Open the completed work order.
2. Add a New Line.
3. Observe the work order status.
column7:
1. The work order status returns to Approved.
2. On the next completion, the modal summarizes already-received vs newly-added parts.
3. When you resolve the last open line again, the work order follows the current settings: with Require Review off it moves to Complete on its own; with Require Review on it moves to Ready for Review.
column8: SV-7697, SV-7870 (S2-R6 / S2 AC (re-open returns to Approved); S16-R12 (auto-complete on re-resolve))

column1: Verify individual-line Complete and per-part receive actions still work alongside Simple completion
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An open work order with multiple lines and a receivable part exists.
column6:
1. Complete one individual line on the work order.
2. Perform a per-part receive action on a line's part.
3. Confirm the line-level Receive button is present.
column7:
1. An individual line can still be completed on its own.
2. The existing per-part receive action still works.
3. A line-level Receive button remains available.
column8: SV-7697 (S2 AC (individual-line Complete + per-part receive kept))

column1: Verify the optional-invoice completion wizard offers Receive Parts, Complete Without Receiving and Cancel
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is OFF (Optional).
3. An open work order with an approved part-bearing line exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the wizard actions.
column7:
1. The wizard shows a Receive step (e.g. 'N parts waiting to receive').
2. The actions are Cancel, Complete Without Receiving, and Receive Parts.
3. If one of the waiting parts is a special-order core, a Resolve cores screen appears before this choice; once every core is decided (OK / Not OK), Complete Without Receiving stays available — only an undecided core blocks completing.

column1: Verify the optional-invoice modal creates POs in the background and shows the count of parts to receive
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is OFF (Optional).
3. An open work order with two approved vendor-part lines exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Read the parts-to-receive count in the modal.
3. Check that POs were created in the background for the vendor parts.
column7:
1. The modal shows the number of parts waiting to receive (e.g. '2 parts waiting to receive').
2. Background POs are created for the vendor parts (a vendorless / sell-price-only part goes on the work order's PO flagged Vendor Missing).
3. All approved-line parts are actually ordered and reach waiting-to-receive, so 'Receive Parts' always has something to receive.
4. No approved part is left in 'requested' and routed to an empty receive screen.
5. Inventory-pick status is reflected in the modal.

column1: Verify Receive Parts opens the shared Accept Delivery page to receive all vendors at once
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the optional-invoice completion wizard for a multi-vendor part work order.
column6:
1. Click Receive Parts.
2. Observe the destination screen.
3. Confirm all vendors' parts appear together.
column7:
1. The shared Accept Delivery page opens.
2. Parts from all vendors are shown for receiving at once.

column1: Verify Complete Without Receiving completes the WO, keeps unreceived parts waiting, and keeps the line Receive button
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the optional-invoice completion wizard with unreceived parts.
column6:
1. Click Complete Without Receiving.
2. Observe the work order status and the Success screen.
3. Reopen the work order and check the unreceived part lines.
column7:
1. The work order completes and the Success screen appears.
2. Unreceived parts remain in a waiting-to-receive state (would show in the Waiting on Parts column).
3. The line still shows a Receive button.
4. Note: a special-order core no longer has to be received first — it is decided (OK / Not OK) on the Resolve cores screen before this choice; only an undecided core blocks Complete Without Receiving.

column1: Verify Cancel closes the completion modal with no change and no duplicate POs on re-open
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the optional-invoice completion wizard (POs already created in the background).
column6:
1. Click Cancel.
2. Reopen the completion wizard by clicking Complete Work Order again.
3. Check the POs for the work order.
column7:
1. Cancel closes the modal with no change to the work order.
2. Re-opening and re-completing does not create duplicate POs (idempotent).

column1: Verify the completion modal collects the missing required vehicle fields (Mileage and Engine Hours; no VIN field in the modal)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Mileage / Engine Hours are ON and the work order is missing those values.
3. You are completing a part-bearing work order with invoice Optional.
4. Require Review Before Completion is off (so VIN is collected at completion, not by the reviewer).
column6:
1. Start completion.
2. Observe the required vehicle fields collected.
3. Leave one empty and try to continue.
column7:
1. When required vehicle fields are missing, the completion Details modal collects Mileage and Engine Hours.
2. There is no VIN field in the completion modal (VIN validity is shown by the 'Valid VIN Required' chip on the work order header; for a review-on work order the VIN is captured later by the reviewer in the Mark Reviewed dialog).
3. You cannot continue until the required fields are supplied (an empty required field shows a 'required field' error).
4. Tech story is handled separately as a line requirement, not inside this step.

column1: Verify the optional-invoice flow reaches the Success screen with WO number and total
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You completed a part-bearing work order via Complete Without Receiving (invoice Optional).
column6:
1. After completing, read the Success screen.
2. Identify the WO number, total, and Go to Invoice / Done buttons.
column7:
1. The Success screen shows the WO number and total.
2. Go to Invoice and Done are available.

column1: Verify the required-invoice wizard disables Complete until parts are received and offers no skip option
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is ON (Required).
3. An open work order with two approved unreceived part lines exists.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the primary CTA state.
3. Look for a 'Complete without receiving' option.
column7:
1. The wizard shows a Receive step ('2 parts waiting to receive').
2. The primary Complete Work Order CTA is DISABLED until all parts are received.
3. There is NO 'Complete without receiving' option.
4. Approved sell-price-only parts (missing vendor and/or cost) are ordered too and reach waiting-to-receive before the receive gate — no approved part is left in 'requested' with nothing to receive.

column1: Verify the required-invoice receive round-trip returns to the modal and enables Complete once all received
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the required-invoice completion wizard with unreceived parts.
column6:
1. Click Receive Parts.
2. On the shared Accept Delivery page, enter qty, tax, date, note and vendor invoice # per vendor and receive all parts.
3. Click Back to Work Order (or finish).
4. Observe the completion modal CTA, then click Complete Work Order.
column7:
1. The receive page collects qty, tax, date, note and invoice # per vendor.
2. On return, once all parts are received the Complete Work Order CTA is enabled.
3. Completing shows the Success screen.
4. Sell-price-only parts were ordered to waiting-to-receive, so they appear in the receive round-trip and are not left in 'requested'.

column1: Verify Cancel in the required-invoice wizard makes no change to the work order
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the required-invoice completion wizard.
column6:
1. Click Cancel.
2. Inspect the work order status and lines.
column7:
1. The modal closes.
2. The work order is unchanged (still not completed).

column1: Verify on a required-invoice work order an unapproved line disables the Complete Work Order button with a tooltip
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is ON (required-invoice / Story 4 flow).
3. Auto-approve Lines is OFF.
4. A work order has one line still in Needs Approval and all other gates satisfied (tech story present, required fields present).
column6:
1. Open the required-invoice work order and start completion.
2. Observe the Complete Work Order button while a line is unapproved.
3. Hover the disabled Complete Work Order button.
4. Approve the line and observe the button again.
column7:
1. In the required-invoice flow (Require Vendor Invoice Number ON), a line still in Needs Approval leaves the Complete Work Order button disabled.
2. Hovering the disabled Complete Work Order button shows the tooltip 'Every line must be approved or declined in order to complete the work order.'
3. The button becomes enabled once every line is approved or declined.
4. In the optional-invoice flow (Require Vendor Invoice Number off) and when Require Review is on, the same unapproved line instead shows the existing message 'you need to approve the line to complete the work order' when you click Complete (the button stays active).
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699 (S4-R8 / Key Decision (all lines approved) / S3-R9)

column1: Verify a manually unapproved line disables the required-invoice Complete Work Order button with a tooltip even when Auto-approve is ON
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is ON (required-invoice / Story 4 flow).
3. Auto-approve Lines is ON.
4. A work order has a line that was manually un-approved after being added.
column6:
1. Confirm one line is unapproved.
2. Start completion and observe the Complete Work Order button.
3. Hover the disabled Complete Work Order button.
4. Re-approve the line and observe the button again.
column7:
1. In the required-invoice flow (Require Vendor Invoice Number ON), a manually un-approved line leaves the Complete Work Order button disabled with the tooltip 'Every line must be approved or declined in order to complete the work order.' — even though Auto-approve Lines is ON.
2. After re-approving every line, the Complete Work Order button enables and completion proceeds.
3. In the optional-invoice flow (Require Vendor Invoice Number off) and when Require Review is on, the same unapproved line instead shows the existing message 'you need to approve the line to complete the work order' when you click Complete.
column8: SV-7699 (S4-R8 / Key Decision (holds regardless of Auto-approve))

column1: Verify re-running completion after a prior attempt does not create duplicate POs
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A part-bearing work order already had completion started once (POs created).
column6:
1. Cancel or exit the first completion attempt.
2. Start completion again.
3. Inspect the POs for the work order at /parts/orders.
column7:
1. Only one PO per vendor exists.
2. No duplicate POs are created by the second completion attempt.

column1: Verify inventory cores are resolved via a line-level Ok/Not-OK control (no distinct Resolve-Cores wizard step)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has an approved inventory line that carries a core charge.
3. Auto-pick is set so the Pick step runs (or picking is otherwise required).
column6:
1. Add a cored inventory part to a work order line and open the line's Parts view.
2. Confirm the part generates a Core sub-line with per-core Ok / Not-OK controls and a $ amount.
3. Click Complete Work Order and step through the completion wizard.
4. Confirm there is no distinct Resolve Cores step and completion goes Details -> Success.
column7:
1. The cored part generates a Core sub-line on the line's Parts view with per-core Ok (returned, no charge) and Not-OK (keep + charge) controls and a $ amount ($0 until Not-OK).
2. The completion wizard has NO distinct Resolve Cores step; a work order whose only remaining action is core resolution completes Details -> Success.
3. Core resolution is a line-level control, not a wizard step.
column8: SV-7698, SV-7699, SV-7870 (S3-C1 / S4-C1 / Resolve Cores handoff)

column1: Verify a work order with no cores completes with no core sub-lines and no Resolve-Cores wizard step
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has no core parts.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Step through the completion wizard.
3. Watch for a Resolve Cores step.
column7:
1. No core sub-lines appear (the work order has no cores).
2. There is no distinct Resolve Cores wizard step; completion proceeds directly Details -> Success.

column1: Verify a Resolve cores screen appears before the Receive parts / Complete without receiving choice and only an undecided core blocks completing
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is OFF (Optional).
3. A work order has a special-order (vendor) cored part that has not been received yet.
column6:
1. On a work order that has an un-received special-order (vendor) cored part, click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the completion wizard steps (Missing Details, Resolve cores, Receive parts & invoice) and open the Resolve cores step.
3. Leave the core undecided and try to move on with Continue.
4. Set the core using OK · Returned or Not OK · Keep + Charge, then try Continue again.
column7:
1. The completion wizard shows a Resolve cores step (before Receive parts & invoice) that lists the un-received vendor core under 'SPECIAL ORDER CORES' with its description, line and core charge, plus OK · Returned / Not OK · Keep + Charge buttons, and the message that resolving now decides whether the core charge is billed (invoice accuracy).
2. While the core is undecided (shows '0 / 1 resolved'), the Continue button is disabled — completion is blocked.
3. Once every core is set (shows '1 / 1 resolved'), Continue is enabled and the wizard proceeds — a decided core no longer blocks moving on (no receive needed first).

column1: Verify the 'Cores pending' indication reflects only undecided special-order cores (a decided core clears it)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A completed (optional-invoice) work order has an un-received special-order core.
column6:
1. With the core still undecided (no OK / Not OK yet), open the work order's invoice / Finance view and look for a cores indication.
2. Decide the core (OK or Not OK) and check again.
column7:
1. While the core is undecided, a 'Cores pending' indication shows and invoice creation is blocked.
2. Once every core is decided (OK or Not OK), the 'Cores pending' indication clears and invoicing is no longer blocked — even though the core part has not been received yet.

column1: Verify the required-invoice flow asks to resolve special-order cores FIRST and then to receive them
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is ON (Required).
3. A work order has a special-order cored part.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the order of the core steps in the wizard.
3. Decide the core OK / Not OK on the resolve screen, then Receive Parts and receive it, then Complete.
column7:
1. The wizard asks to resolve the core FIRST (same resolve screen as the optional flow) and then to receive — not resolve-after-receive.
2. At receive the saved decision is applied automatically; the user is not asked OK / Not OK again.
3. After all parts are received, Complete succeeds to the Success screen.

column1: Verify the completion and invoice gates detect an undecided special-order core that exists only as a requested part
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has a special-order cored part that exists only as a part request (not received, no work-order part yet) and is still undecided.
column6:
1. Try to complete the work order and to create the invoice.
2. Decide the core OK / Not OK and try again.
column7:
1. The undecided core is detected even though it exists only as a requested (un-received) part — completing and invoicing are blocked.
2. Once the core is decided, the gates clear (no receive needed first).

column1: Verify the core '+$ to invoice' amount is shown at the line level as a core is marked Not-OK (no Resolve-Cores wizard total)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are in the Resolve Cores step with multiple cores.
column6:
1. On the line's Parts view, mark a Core sub-line Not-OK (keep + charge).
2. Observe the $ amount on that Core sub-line.
3. Mark the core Ok and observe the $ amount again.
column7:
1. The Core sub-line shows a $ amount on the line's Parts view ($0 until it is marked Not-OK).
2. Marking the core Not-OK sets the +$ to invoice on that line.
3. There is no distinct Resolve Cores wizard step with a running total; the core $ is a line-level control.

column1: Verify the Resolve cores screen lists every un-received vendor core with part info, core charge and OK / Not OK, plus an invoice-accuracy message
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Vendor Invoice Number is OFF (Optional).
3. A work order has two special-order (vendor) cored parts that have not been received yet.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the screen shown right before the Receive parts / Complete without receiving choice.
3. Read the message on the screen.
column7:
1. A consolidated Resolve cores step appears under a 'SPECIAL ORDER CORES · N' group, listing every un-received vendor core.
2. Each core shows its description, line and core charge with OK · Returned / Not OK · Keep + Charge buttons.
3. The message 'core part can now be resolved — mark whether each old unit was returned. This decides whether the core charge is billed.' explains the resolution is for invoice accuracy.

column1: Verify marking a core Not OK immediately adds the core charge to the work order total and customer invoice, while OK adds no charge
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has two un-received vendor cores shown on the Resolve cores screen.
column6:
1. Mark one core Not OK and note the work order total.
2. Mark the other core OK and note the total again.
3. Create the customer invoice and check its amounts.
column7:
1. Not OK: the core charge is priced into the work order total right away and flows to the customer invoice.
2. OK: no charge is added (the vendor core return is created automatically later, at receive).
3. The invoice matches the decisions even though no core part has been received.

column1: Verify completion and invoice creation are blocked only while a core is undecided — a decided core does not block
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has two un-received vendor cores.
column6:
1. Decide one core (OK or Not OK), leave the other undecided; try to complete the work order and to create the invoice.
2. Decide the remaining core and try again.
column7:
1. With any core still undecided, completing and invoice creation are blocked and a cores-pending indication shows.
2. Once every core is decided, completion and invoice creation proceed — no receive is required first.

column1: Verify receiving a pre-resolved core auto-applies the saved decision: OK creates exactly one vendor return, Not OK creates none, the invoice never changes, retries create no duplicates
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has one core pre-resolved OK and another pre-resolved Not OK, both not yet received; the customer invoice is created.
column6:
1. Receive the OK core; check vendor returns and the customer invoice.
2. Receive the Not OK core; check again.
3. Retry / re-submit the receive and re-check for duplicates.
column7:
1. The OK core is received already resolved, with exactly ONE vendor core return created automatically.
2. The Not OK core is received already resolved, with NO return created.
3. The user is never asked OK / Not OK again, the customer invoice does not change at receive, and retries create no duplicate cores or returns.

column1: Verify the receive dialog locks quantity to the full remaining amount once the work order is invoiced/paid, with the core auto-selected and an explanatory tooltip
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. An invoiced/paid work order has an un-received cored part; another (not yet invoiced) work order also has one.
column6:
1. Open the receive dialog for the invoiced/paid work order's part, try to change the quantity, and hover the field.
2. Open the receive dialog for the not-yet-invoiced work order's part and change the quantity.
column7:
1. On the invoiced/paid work order the quantity is locked to the full remaining amount, the core is auto-selected, and the tooltip reads 'This part is on a customer invoice and should be received in full'.
2. Before invoicing, the quantity stays editable (partial receive allowed).
3. The lock is on the screen only — the customer invoice itself never changes at receive.

column1: Verify the Lines tab shows the core decision state before and after receive: 'Core decision pending', 'Core OK — return to vendor, no charge', 'Core Not OK — customer charged'
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has three vendor cores: one undecided, one decided OK, one decided Not OK.
column6:
1. Open the work order's Lines tab before receiving and read each core's state.
2. Receive the two decided cores and re-check the Lines tab.
column7:
1. Before receive: the undecided core shows 'Core decision pending'; the OK core shows 'Core OK — return to vendor, no charge'; the Not OK core shows 'Core Not OK — customer charged'.
2. After receive, a pre-resolved core shows its resolved state with NO OK / Not OK buttons.
3. No duplicate core prompts appear anywhere.

column1: Verify a core decision cannot be changed once the work order has an active invoice
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has a decided core and an active customer invoice.
column6: 1. Try to change the core's OK / Not OK decision (on the resolve screen or the Lines tab).
column7: 1. The decision cannot be changed while the work order has an active invoice.
column8: SV-8353 (S18 AC (resolution immutable with an active invoice))

column1: API: Verify POST /api/work-orders/{id}/pre-resolve-cores persists the core decision on the part request with no side-effect records
column5:
1. A valid Admin session (API).
2. A work order with an un-received special-order cored part request exists.
column6:
1. POST /api/work-orders/{id}/pre-resolve-cores with body {cores:[{partRequestId, isCoreOk}]} (isCoreOk true = OK/Returned, false = Not OK).
2. Re-read the work order lines read model and check the core part request's core_resolution and the pending-core count.
3. Inspect for side-effect records (work-order part, statement item, vendor return, order).
column7:
1. The request succeeds (201) returning {data:{resolvedCount:N}} and core_resolution is persisted on the core part request (ok | not_ok; NULL = undecided; isCoreOk cannot be null).
2. NO WorkOrderPart, statement item, vendor return or order is created — part request stays authorized_to_order with quantity_remaining and total_core_charge unchanged.
3. cores_pending reflects only undecided (NULL) cores after the call (decided cores drop out).

column1: API: Verify resolving a received core via the existing handle-core endpoints also writes the decision back to the linked core part request
column5:
1. A valid Admin session (API).
2. A received cored part exists that can be resolved via the existing handle-core(s) endpoints.
column6:
1. Resolve the received core Ok / Not OK via the existing handle-core(s) endpoint.
2. Read the linked core part request and its core_resolution value.
column7: 1. The call succeeds and the decision is ALSO written to the linked core PartRequest (core_resolution matches the handle-core decision), keeping core_resolution the single source of history.

column1: Verify each work order line shows a Story sub-row with an 'Add tech story for this line' link when empty
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Tech Story is ON.
3. A work order has a line with no tech story yet.
column6:
1. Open the work order Lines tab.
2. Look under the line for a Story sub-row.
column7:
1. The line has a Story sub-row.
2. When empty, it shows an 'Add tech story for this line' link.

column1: Verify with Require tech story ON every line needs a story before the work order can complete
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Tech Story is ON.
3. A work order has at least one line missing a story.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe whether completion proceeds without stories.
column7:
1. Completion cannot proceed while any line is missing a tech story.
2. The user is routed to enter the missing stories first.

column1: Verify Complete opens the tech-story modal first and then chains into completion (order: tech story → parts → complete)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Tech Story is ON.
3. A work order has a line missing a story.
column6:
1. Click Complete Work Order.
2. Observe the first modal that appears.
3. Enter a story and click Continue.
4. Observe the next step.
column7:
1. The tech-story modal opens FIRST (before the completion wizard).
2. After Continue, the flow chains into the completion wizard (parts/pick → complete).
3. Gate order is tech story → parts → complete/send-to-review.

column1: Verify the tech-story modal structure (header, per-line card, Line X of N, required textarea, disabled Next)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The tech-story modal is open during completion.
column6:
1. Read the modal header.
2. Read the per-line card (line #, name, technician).
3. Read the 'Line X of N' indicator.
4. Leave the textarea empty and check the Next/Continue button.
column7:
1. The header reads 'Tech story' with 'WO# · Customer'.
2. A per-line card shows the line number, name and technician; a 'Line X of N' indicator is shown.
3. The Next/Continue button is disabled until the textarea is non-empty.

column1: Verify multi-line tech-story navigation (Back after line 1, Continue/Save on the last line)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has two or more lines all missing stories, and Require Tech Story is ON.
column6:
1. Start completion so the tech-story modal opens on Line 1 of N.
2. Enter a story and click Next.
3. On line 2, check for a Back button.
4. On the last line, check the final button.
column7:
1. On line 1 there is no Back button; after line 1, a Back button appears.
2. Each line requires a non-empty story to advance.
3. The last line shows Continue (chained into completion) or Save.

column1: Verify a saved tech story renders inline with a green check, the text and an Edit link
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A line has a saved tech story.
column6:
1. View the line's Story sub-row.
2. Confirm the story text and controls.
column7:
1. The saved story renders inline with a green check and the story text.
2. An Edit link is available to change it.

column1: Verify the tech-story modal has a text box for typing the story
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The tech-story modal is open.
column6:
1. Open the tech-story modal on a line.
2. Locate the text box where the story is typed.
3. Type a story into the text box.
column7:
1. The tech-story modal has a text box (textarea) for the story.
2. The story text you type is accepted in the box.

column1: Verify tech story is captured both inline and via the gate modal (Story 17 supersedes on-the-line-only wording)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has a line missing a story.
column6:
1. Add a tech story inline via the line's 'Add tech story' link.
2. On a separate line missing a story, trigger the gate modal by clicking Complete.
3. Confirm both entry points save a story.
column7:
1. A tech story can be entered inline on the line (Story 17 is the authoritative behavior).
2. A story can also be entered via the completion gate modal, which lets stories be completed individually or several at once.
3. Both paths persist the story.

column1: Verify a vendorless part can be requested with description, quantity and category (part number, cost, vendor and sell price left empty)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin at https://sv7301.qa.shopview.com.
2. An open work order with a line is on its Lines tab.
column6:
1. Add a part to a line.
2. Enter a description, a quantity and a category.
3. Leave part number, cost, vendor and sell price empty.
4. Save the part.
column7:
1. The part saves successfully with description, quantity and category entered; part number, cost, vendor and sell price may be left empty.
2. Category is a required field for v1 — the part cannot be saved without a category.
3. Sell price is not enforced as required for v1 — the part can be saved without a sell price.
4. The part appears on the line with its description and quantity and is treated as a vendorless part downstream; it is orderable from the line (Order creates or joins the Vendor-Missing purchase order and moves it to waiting-to-receive).

column1: Verify adding a part is blocked when description, quantity or category is missing (sell price not enforced)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The add-part dialog is open on a work order line.
column6:
1. Leave the description empty and try to save.
2. Fill the description, leave the quantity empty and try to save.
3. Fill the description and quantity, leave the category empty and try to save.
4. Fill the description, quantity and category but leave the sell price empty and try to save.
column7:
1. Saving is blocked inline when the description is empty ('Description is a required field').
2. Saving is blocked inline when the quantity is empty ('Quantity is a required field').
3. Saving is blocked inline when the category is empty ('Category is a required field').
4. Saving is allowed when only the sell price is empty — sell price is not enforced as a required field for v1.

column1: Verify a vendorless part's type uses the existing source field (vendor or found) and never inventory
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A vendorless part has been added to a work order line.
column6:
1. Open the vendorless part's detail.
2. Read its source / type field.
column7:
1. The source is 'vendor' or 'found'.
2. It is never set to 'inventory'.
3. It is treated as vendorless downstream.

column1: Verify a vendorless part is editable after creation
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A vendorless part exists on a work order line.
column6:
1. Open the vendorless part.
2. Change its description or quantity and save.
column7:
1. The part can be edited after creation.
2. The changes persist.

column1: Verify a no-part-number part creates no inventory item and no Part History
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A part with description + qty + sell but no part number exists on a work order.
column6:
1. Search inventory for a new item matching the description.
2. Check for any Part History entry for it.
column7:
1. No inventory item is created for the no-PN part.
2. No Part History is written until a part number is added.

column1: Verify adding a part number and vendor later transitions the part out of vendorless
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A vendorless part (no PN, no vendor) exists on a work order.
column6:
1. Edit the part and add a part number.
2. Assign a vendor to it.
3. Observe the part's vendorless status.
column7:
1. Once both a part number and a vendor are present, the part is no longer treated as vendorless.
2. It becomes eligible for downstream inventory / QuickBooks handling.

column1: Verify a vendorless / no-PN part cannot be received until a part number (and vendor) is entered
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A vendorless / no-PN part is on a work order PO.
column6:
1. Open a receive surface (Accept Delivery / Bulk Receive) for that PO.
2. Attempt to receive the part without a part number.
3. Attempt to receive it without a vendor.
column7:
1. Receiving is blocked while the part number is missing.
2. Receiving is blocked while the vendor is missing.
3. Receiving is enabled only after both a part number and a vendor are provided.

column1: Verify a vendorless vendor-part goes onto the work order's normal PO with no separate dummy PO
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has a vendor part with no vendor assigned and Create POs is on.
3. The work order has been completed so POs are generated.
column6:
1. Open the PO list at /parts/orders.
2. Find the PO for this work order.
3. Confirm the vendorless part is on that PO.
column7:
1. The vendorless part is placed on the work order's normal PO.
2. No separate 'dummy PO' is created for it.

column1: Verify a 'Vendor Missing +N' indication shows on the PO list and PO detail
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A PO exists that holds a part with no vendor.
column6:
1. Open /parts/orders.
2. Look for the Vendor Missing indication on the PO row.
3. Open the PO detail and confirm the indication there.
column7:
1. The PO list shows a 'Vendor Missing' indication (with '+N' when multiple vendors are involved).
2. The PO detail also shows the Vendor Missing flag.

column1: Verify a Vendor Missing PO is flagged and excluded from QuickBooks sync
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A Vendor Missing PO exists.
3. QuickBooks integration is available for inspection.
column6:
1. Trigger / inspect QuickBooks sync for the PO.
2. Confirm the Vendor Missing PO is excluded.
column7:
1. The Vendor Missing PO is flagged.
2. It is excluded from QuickBooks sync while the vendor is missing.

column1: Verify a Vendor Missing PO offers options to select a vendor and enter/edit the part number
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A Vendor Missing PO detail is open.
column6:
1. Open the PO detail.
2. Look for a way to select a vendor.
3. Look for a way to enter/edit the missing part number.
column7:
1. The Vendor Missing PO detail offers a way to select a vendor.
2. It offers a way to enter or edit the part number.

column1: Verify the Vendor Missing flag clears once both a vendor and a part number are provided
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A Vendor Missing PO exists with a part lacking vendor and part number.
column6:
1. Assign a vendor to the PO.
2. Enter the missing part number.
3. Observe the Vendor Missing flag.
column7:
1. Once both a vendor and a part number are provided the Vendor Missing flag is removed.
2. The part becomes eligible for QuickBooks.

column1: Verify a Vendor Missing PO's spend is excluded from the QuickBooks Vendor Bill export and the Vendors Expenses report until a vendor is assigned
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A Vendor Missing PO with a non-zero cost exists.
column6:
1. Open the Vendors Expenses report and look for the vendor-missing PO's spend.
2. Inspect the QuickBooks Vendor Bill export for that PO.
3. Assign a vendor to the PO and check both again.
column7:
1. While the PO has no vendor, its spend is NOT counted in the Vendors Expenses report.
2. Its spend is excluded from the QuickBooks Vendor Bill export.
3. There is no dedicated purchase-order report and no 'needs vendor' marker — nothing 'marks' these POs.
4. Once a vendor is assigned, the spend flows into both normally.

column1: Verify a sell-price-only part is orderable from the line's Order action, joins the Vendor-Missing PO and moves to waiting-to-receive
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin at https://sv7301.qa.shopview.com.
2. An open work order has a sell-price-only line part (sell price set; vendor and/or cost missing; part number empty).
column6:
1. On the line, use the Order action for the sell-price-only part.
2. Open the PO list at /parts/orders and find the work order's PO.
3. Confirm the part's status.
column7:
1. Ordering from the line creates or joins the work order's Vendor-Missing PO (no separate dummy PO).
2. The part moves from 'requested' to 'waiting-to-receive' without completing the work order.
3. At receive, a vendor and part number are still required (cost editable — Story 10).

column1: Verify the PO list has a select-all checkbox and per-PO checkboxes
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The PO list at /parts/orders has multiple POs.
column6:
1. Open /parts/orders.
2. Look for a select-all checkbox in the header.
3. Look for a checkbox on each PO row.
column7:
1. A select-all checkbox is present.
2. Each PO row has its own checkbox.

column1: Verify selecting POs shows a bar with 'N purchase orders selected', Clear and Receive Selected
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The PO list has selectable POs.
column6:
1. Select one or more POs.
2. Observe the action bar.
column7:
1. A bar appears reading 'N purchase orders selected'.
2. The bar has Clear and Receive Selected actions.

column1: Verify Receive Selected opens the PO Bulk Receive page carrying the selected POs
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Two or more POs are selected on the PO list.
column6:
1. Click Receive Selected.
2. Observe the destination page and the POs shown.
column7:
1. The PO Bulk Receive page opens (Story 8).
2. It contains the POs that were selected.

column1: Verify fulfilled (already-received) POs are not selectable
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The PO list contains at least one fulfilled PO.
column6: 1. Attempt to select a fulfilled PO's checkbox.
column7: 1. The fulfilled PO cannot be selected (checkbox disabled).

column1: Verify Vendor Missing POs are selectable and clearly indicated in the list
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The PO list contains a Vendor Missing PO.
column6:
1. Select a Vendor Missing PO.
2. Confirm its Vendor Missing indication is shown while selected.
column7:
1. The Vendor Missing PO is selectable.
2. Its Vendor Missing status remains clearly indicated.

column1: Verify select-all only toggles POs on the current page/filter
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The PO list has more POs than fit on one page (or a filter is applied).
column6:
1. Apply a filter or page the list.
2. Click select-all.
3. Check which POs are selected.
column7: 1. Select-all only selects POs in the current page/filter, not the whole dataset.

column1: Verify part-sale-originated POs appear in the PO list and are selectable like work-order POs
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A Part Sale with a vendor part exists, so a part-sale purchase order was created.
column6:
1. Open the Purchase Orders list and find the part-sale PO.
2. Select it (checkbox) together with work-order POs and use Receive Selected.
column7:
1. The part-sale-originated PO appears in the PO list.
2. It is selectable and joins the Receive Selected flow like a work-order PO.
column8: SV-7702 (S7 AC (part-sale POs) + §8 Part Sales — confirmed)

column1: Verify the Bulk Receive page has a 'Back To Purchase Orders' link that returns to the PO list
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You reached the Bulk Receive page via Receive Selected.
column6:
1. Locate the top-left 'Back To Purchase Orders' link.
2. Click it.
column7:
1. A 'Back To Purchase Orders' link is present top-left.
2. Clicking it returns to the PO list.

column1: Verify the Bulk Receive page groups POs by vendor with a vendor count and per-vendor expand/collapse
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Multiple POs across multiple vendors were sent to the Bulk Receive page.
column6:
1. Read the vendor group headers and counts.
2. Use one vendor's Expand/Collapse all control.
3. Confirm each vendor has its own control (not one global).
column7:
1. POs are grouped by vendor with a count per vendor.
2. Each vendor group has its own Expand/Collapse all control.
3. POs within a group are collapsible.

column1: Verify each PO row shows the PO number, related work order (or inventory/no-WO indicator) and parts count
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The Bulk Receive page is open with several POs.
column6: 1. Read a PO row's details.
column7:
1. The row shows the PO number.
2. It shows the related work order, or an inventory / no-WO indicator.
3. It shows the parts count.

column1: Verify selection behavior: nothing selected by default; selecting a PO selects all its parts; individual parts selectable; actions locked until checked
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The Bulk Receive page is open with POs and parts.
column6:
1. Confirm nothing is selected on load.
2. Select a PO and confirm all its parts get selected.
3. Deselect an individual part.
4. Confirm the receive action is locked when nothing is checked.
column7:
1. Nothing is selected by default.
2. Selecting a PO selects all its parts; individual parts can be toggled.
3. Actions are locked until at least one item is checked.

column1: Verify the per-PO 'Receive parts (N)' button is disabled until a vendor invoice number is entered
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A PO's parts are selected on the Bulk Receive page.
column6:
1. Confirm the 'Receive parts (N)' button state with no invoice number.
2. Enter a vendor invoice number.
3. Confirm the button state again.
column7:
1. The Receive button is disabled without a vendor invoice number.
2. For a vendor-missing PO it also requires a vendor assigned and the missing part number entered.
3. Once satisfied, the Receive button enables.

column1: Verify Bulk Receive field editability: quantity editable (partial receive), cost editable ONLY when it is $0, sell locks after the WO is invoiced/paid
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The Bulk Receive page has a part whose cost is $0, a part whose cost is not $0, and a PO whose work order IS invoiced/paid.
column6:
1. Edit the quantity on a part (partial receive).
2. Try to edit the cost on the part whose cost is $0.
3. Try to edit the cost on the part whose cost is not $0.
4. On the invoiced/paid PO, try to edit the sell price and hover the locked field.
column7:

column7:

2. A 'Ready for Review' / 'Sent for review' indication is shown.

4. The same Review / Ready-for-Review end state is reached when the last open line auto-resolves under Require Review on, not only when Send To Review is clicked explicitly.

column1: Verify the Mark Reviewed dialog captures VIN (required) and disables Confirm until VIN is entered

column6:
1. Click Mark Reviewed.
2. Observe the VIN field.
3. Clear the VIN and check the Confirm Review button, then enter a VIN.
column7:
1. The Mark Reviewed dialog shows a VIN / Serial # field, required if the work order is missing a valid VIN.
2. Confirm Review is disabled until a VIN is present.
3. Once a VIN is entered, Confirm Review is enabled.

column1: Verify on Send to Review lines lock to Complete and inventory is auto-picked
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order with an inventory line just went to Review.
column6:
1. Open the work order in Review state.
2. Check the line states.
3. Check whether inventory was auto-picked.
column7:
1. Lines are locked to Complete.
2. Inventory has been auto-picked.

column1: Verify Confirm Review signs off and completes the work order directly (no distinct Reviewed holding state)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order is in Review with the Mark Reviewed dialog filled (VIN present).
column6:
1. Click Confirm Review.
2. Observe the resulting work order state.
3. Look for a separate final 'Complete Work Order' action.
column7:
1. After Confirm Review the sign-off completes and the work order moves directly Review -> Complete.
2. There is no distinct 'Reviewed' holding state and no separate final 'Complete Work Order' click.
3. Note: with Require Review on, resolving the last open line first routes the work order to Ready for Review; sign-off (Confirm Review) then moves it to Complete.
column8: SV-7870 (R5 / R8 (direct sign-off, no separate Complete) + S16-R12)

column1: Verify Mark Reviewed is gated by the Review Work Orders permission and disabled for a role without it
column5:
1. A role with Review Work Orders and a role without it both exist.
2. A work order is in Review state, sent to review by a known user.
column6:
1. Sign in as a role without Review Work Orders and open the work order in Review.
2. Confirm Mark Reviewed is disabled with 'Awaiting review'.
3. Sign in as a role with Review Work Orders (system defaults grant it broadly; it can be limited to manager/foreman via custom roles) and confirm Mark Reviewed is available.
column7:
1. A role without the Review Work Orders permission sees Mark Reviewed disabled with an 'Awaiting review' indicator.
2. A role with the Review Work Orders permission can Mark Reviewed and sign off.
3. A user who holds the Review Work Orders permission may Mark Reviewed a work order they completed themselves — self-review is allowed in v1 with NO reviewer != completer identity restriction (the gate is purely the permission).

column1: Verify the Mark Reviewed dialog includes VIN / Serial # (required) with no review note field
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. The Mark Reviewed dialog is open.
column6:
1. Open the Mark Reviewed dialog.
2. Confirm a required VIN / Serial # field (Confirm disabled until VIN entered).
3. Confirm there is no review note field, then complete the sign-off.
column7:
1. The Mark Reviewed dialog shows a VIN / Serial # field that is required (Confirm Reviewed is disabled until VIN is entered).
2. There is no review note field on the dialog.
3. The sign-off completes using the VIN / Serial # only.

column1: Verify sign-off completes the work order directly (no separate final Complete) and invoicing is blocked until reviewed
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order is in Reviewed state (or a Review state before sign-off for the invoicing-block check).
column6:
1. Before sign-off, attempt to invoice the work order.
2. Complete the review sign-off (Confirm Review).
3. Confirm the work order becomes Complete (invoice-ready).
column7:
1. Invoicing is blocked until the work order is reviewed.
2. After sign-off the work order moves directly Review -> Complete (invoice-ready), with no separate final Complete Work Order click.
3. With Require Review on the work order never auto-completes on last-line-resolve; it routes to Ready for Review and invoicing stays blocked until it is reviewed.

column1: Verify a 'Ready for Review' list filter/column surfaces the reviewer queue
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. At least one work order is in Review state.
column6:
1. Open the Work Orders list.
2. Look for a 'Ready for Review' filter or column.
3. Confirm work orders in Review appear in it.
column7: 1. A 'Ready for Review' filter/column lists work orders awaiting review.

column1: Verify all lines must be approved before Send To Review (the 'Send To Review' action is disabled until every line is approved)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Review is ON and a work order has one unapproved line.
column6:
1. Open the work order and locate the 'Send To Review' action while a line is still unapproved.
2. Attempt to use Send To Review with the unapproved line.
column7: 1. The 'Send To Review' action cannot be used while any line is unapproved - the 'Send To Review' button is disabled until every line has been approved.

column1: Verify cores are decided before receiving ahead of Send to Review, and invoicing stays blocked until Reviewed and every core is decided
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. Require Review is ON and a work order has inventory and special-order cores.
column6:
1. Resolve inventory cores in the completion modal (after Pick) before Send to Review.
2. Decide the special-order cores OK / Not OK on the resolve screen BEFORE receiving, before Send to Review (same in required- and optional-invoice flows).
3. Attempt to invoice before the work order is Reviewed and before every core is decided.
column7:
1. Inventory cores are resolved before Send to Review.
2. Special-order cores are pre-resolved before receiving on the resolve screen before Send to Review — no longer deferred to the Create Invoice gate.
3. Invoicing is blocked until the work order is Reviewed AND every core is decided; only an undecided core blocks — a decided (un-received) core does not.

column1: Verify Require Review Before Completion starts ON for a brand-new organization, and existing organizations keep today's behavior
column5:
1. A brand-new organization / account (no settings changed yet) and an existing organization are available.
2. Signed in as Admin for each.
column6:
1. On a brand-new organization, open Settings > Work Orders and check the Require Review Before Completion setting.
2. On an existing organization, confirm its completion behavior is unchanged (the setting is backfilled).
column7:
1. On a brand-new organization / account, Require Review Before Completion defaults to ON (Milos decision, 2026-07-16: it stays ON for every new organization).
2. Existing organizations keep their current completion behavior (the setting is backfilled so their behavior does not change).
column8: SV-7870 (R Open (default) - Milos Round-3 2026-07-16: ON for new orgs)

column1: Verify the work order primary button reads 'Create Work Order'
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. You are on the Create Work Order form (/workorders → Create).
column6:
1. Open the Create Work Order form.
2. Read the primary button label.
column7: 1. The primary button reads 'Create Work Order'.

column1: Verify required fields at completion appear in a centralized center modal and the tech story is NOT in that modal
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order requiring mileage/VIN is being completed.
column6:
1. Start completion.
2. Observe where required fields are collected.
3. Confirm the tech story is handled by its own flow, not inside this modal.
column7:
1. The required vehicle fields (Mileage and Engine Hours) are collected in a centralized center modal titled 'Complete Work Order'.
2. The tech story is NOT part of this modal (it is handled by its own line-level flow).

column1: Verify the success screen shows WO number and total with Done and Go to Invoice, and the invoice number is on the Finance step
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A work order has just been completed.
column6:
1. Read the success screen.
2. Confirm WO number, total, Done and Go to Invoice.
3. Confirm the invoice number is shown on the Finance step, not the success screen.
column7:
1. The success screen shows the WO number and total with Done and Go to Invoice.
2. The invoice number appears on the Finance step, not on the success screen.

column1: Verify the close-confirmation modal behavior (Close = closes modal only; Cancel = closes modal + returns to previous screen)
column5:
1. Signed in as Admin.
2. A completion modal is open.
column6:
1. Trigger the close-confirmation modal.
2. Click Close (prominent/red) and observe.
3. Trigger it again and click Cancel (text link, far left) and observe.
column7:
1. Close (prominent/red button) closes the confirmation modal only, discards nothing (no discard warning), and stays on the work order.
2. Cancel (text link, far left) closes the modal and returns to the previous screen.
3. Other consumers of the shared confirmation dialog keep their existing action labels.

column1: Verify only owner/admin can view and modify Work Order settings (non-admin blocked)
column5:
1. A role with the App Settings permission (e.g. Admin) and a role without it (e.g. Service Advisor or Technician) both exist.
2. You can sign in as each.
column6:
1. Sign in as a role with App Settings and open and modify /administration/settings → Work Orders.
2. Sign in as a role without App Settings and attempt to open and modify the same page.
3. As the role without App Settings, attempt to save a Work Order settings change directly (API), and note the response.
column7:
1. Only a role with the App Settings permission (system defaults Admin, Service Manager and Office) can view and modify the Work Order settings page.
2. A role without App Settings cannot open or change the Work Order settings.
3. The backend rejects a Work Order settings save attempted by a role that lacks App Settings.

column1: Verify which roles can complete a work order (Simple completion)
column5:
1. Credentials for several roles exist.
2. A work order ready to complete exists.
column6:
1. For each role, attempt to complete a work order.
2. Record which roles can and cannot.
column7:
1. Roles with Work Orders: Create & Edit plus WO Lines: Create & Edit and Full View (needed to approve all lines) can complete a work order: Admin, Service Manager, Senior SA, Service Advisor, Foreman and Parts Manager.
2. Technician and Parts Tech cannot complete (Technician cannot approve lines in Tech View and/or lacks Work Orders: Create & Edit; Parts Tech is a receiver, not a completer).
3. Office, Sales Rep and Time Clock cannot complete a work order.

column1: Verify which roles can perform Bulk Receive
column5:
1. Credentials for several roles exist.
2. The Bulk Receive flow is available (Story 7/8 built).
column6:
1. For each role, attempt to reach and use Bulk Receive.
2. Record the outcomes.
column7:
1. Roles with Vendor & Order Mgmt: Create & Edit plus See Financial Data can reach and use Bulk Receive: Admin, Service Manager, Senior SA, Service Advisor, Foreman, Parts Manager and Parts Tech.
2. Office (Vendor & Order Mgmt: View only) can open the Bulk Receive page but cannot receive.
3. Sales Rep and Time Clock cannot reach Bulk Receive.

column1: Verify which roles can Mark Reviewed (sign off)
column5:
1. Credentials for roles with and without Review Work Orders exist.
2. A work order in Review state exists, sent to review by a known user.
column6:
1. For each role, attempt to Mark Reviewed.
2. Record which roles can and cannot.
column7:
1. Mark Reviewed (review sign-off) requires the Review Work Orders permission; system defaults grant it broadly, and it can be narrowed to manager/foreman via custom roles.
2. A role without Review Work Orders sees Mark Reviewed disabled with an 'Awaiting review' indicator.
3. A user who holds the Review Work Orders / Mark Reviewed permission may Mark Reviewed a work order they completed themselves — self-review is allowed in v1. There is NO reviewer != completer identity restriction; the gate is purely the permission.

column1: Verify the PO Receive button is hidden for office/readonly users
column5:
1. An Office / read-only credential (no Order Parts) exists.
2. A WO-originated PO exists, plus a fulfilled PO.
column6:
1. Sign in as an Office / read-only user.
2. Open the PO list and detail.
3. Confirm the Receive action is not shown, and confirm it is also absent on a fulfilled PO.
column7:
1. The Receive action requires the Order Parts permission; Office and read-only users (no Order Parts) do not see Receive on the PO list or PO detail.
2. Receive is also hidden for fulfilled (already-received) POs.

column1: Verify permission gating of Simple-Flow settings and work-order actions (UI gating is the v1 pass criterion)
column5:
1. Signed in with API access.
2. A relevant Simple-Flow setting (e.g. Require Vendor Invoice Number) is ON.
column6:
1. As a role that lacks the mapped permission, confirm the gated setting or action is hidden or unavailable in the app.
2. As that same role, try the same setting change directly through the API (bypassing the app) and note the response.
3. As a role that lacks the completion or review sign-off permission, try to complete a work order and to sign off a review directly through the API and note the responses.
4. As a role that only has Work Orders: Create & Edit, try to receive parts onto a work order through the API and note the response.
column7:
1. In the app, a role without the mapped permission does not see or cannot use the gated setting or action (this is the v1 pass criterion).
2. The Work Order settings save is also blocked at the backend: the unauthorized API request is rejected with HTTP 403.
3. Work order completion and review sign-off are NOT blocked at the backend today: a direct API call from a role lacking the permission still succeeds (HTTP 200). This still passes v1 on the app-level restriction, but the backend gap is a known issue to fix later — note it as 'app blocks / backend allows'.
4. Because several work-order permissions share the same backend check, any role with Work Orders: Create & Edit can receive parts onto a work order through the API.

column1: Verify review sign-off is governed by the Review Work Orders custom-role permission (not open to all)
column5:
1. Credentials for roles with and without Review Work Orders exist.
2. A work order in Review state exists, sent to review by a known user.
column6: 1. Confirm that only roles holding Review Work Orders can sign off, and roles without it cannot.
column7:
1. Review sign-off is governed by the Review Work Orders custom-role permission (it is NOT open to all users for v1).
2. The permission gates the Mark Reviewed action (a role without Review Work Orders cannot sign off; a role with it can).
3. A user who holds the Review Work Orders permission may sign off a work order they completed themselves — self-review is allowed in v1 with NO reviewer != completer identity restriction (the gate is purely the permission).

column1: Verify a user who holds the Mark Reviewed permission can Mark Reviewed a work order they completed
column5:
1. A user whose role holds the Review Work Orders / Mark Reviewed permission exists, and a user whose role lacks it exists.
2. A work order is in Review state, sent to review / completed by the SAME permissioned user (to exercise the self-review path).
column6:
1. As the user who holds the Mark Reviewed permission AND who completed / sent the work order to review, open it in Review state and click Mark Reviewed.
2. Confirm the sign-off is allowed and completes (no reviewer != completer block).
3. As a user whose role does NOT hold the Mark Reviewed permission, open a work order in Review and check the Mark Reviewed control.
column7:
1. A user who holds the Review Work Orders / Mark Reviewed permission CAN Mark Reviewed a work order they completed themselves — self-review is allowed in v1 (there is NO reviewer != completer identity restriction).
2. A user whose role does NOT hold the Mark Reviewed permission cannot sign off — the Mark Reviewed control is disabled with an 'Awaiting review' indicator.
3. The only gate on Mark Reviewed is the Review Work Orders permission; who completed the work order is irrelevant.
column8: SV-7870 (R7 (review sign-off) — self-review permission-gated (identity rule NOT in v1))

column1: Verify a Technician cannot add a vendorless / no-part-number part (lacks See Financial Data)
column5:
1. A Technician credential exists (WO Lines: Create & Edit, no See Financial Data).
2. An open work order with a line is available.
column6:
1. Sign in as the Technician and open the work order line.
2. Attempt to add a vendorless / no-part-number part (description + quantity + sell price).
column7:
1. The Technician cannot add a vendorless / no-part-number part.
2. The mandatory sell price cannot be entered without See Financial Data, so the add is prevented.

column1: Verify the Complete Work Order action follows the per-role completion permission matrix
column5:
1. Credentials for each system role exist (Admin, Service Manager, Senior SA, Service Advisor, Foreman, Technician, Parts Manager, Parts Tech, Office, Sales Rep, Time Clock).
2. A work order ready to complete is available.
column6:
1. For each role, open the work order and check whether the Complete Work Order action is available and usable.
2. Record the result per role against the checklist below.
3. Roles expected to be able to complete: Admin, Service Manager, Senior SA, Service Advisor, Foreman, Parts Manager.
4. Roles expected NOT to be able to complete: Technician, Parts Tech, Office, Sales Rep, Time Clock.
column7:
1. Complete Work Order is available for Admin, Service Manager, Senior SA, Service Advisor, Foreman and Parts Manager.
2. Complete Work Order is NOT available for Technician, Parts Tech, Office, Sales Rep or Time Clock.
3. Technician and Parts Tech are blocked because they cannot approve lines and/or lack Work Orders: Create & Edit; Office is view-only; Sales Rep and Time Clock have no work-order edit access.

column1: Verify completion is blocked when required mileage is missing
column5:
